guards.maps_to: events/tanx.py:27-31 counts InstinctEnchantment.can_enchant over the deck and compares against TriBoomerang.MIN_ELIGIBLE. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes_a.py reacha`): MIN_ELIGIBLE is 3, the source's `_triBoomerangCount` (Tanx.cs:21). The threshold lives on the relic in the sim rather than inline, the same placement the nonupeipe record recorded for Beautiful Bracelet. Instinct's CanEnchant is audited under enchantment/instinct.

events/tanx.py:34-35 shuffles in place then slices [:3]. The primitive is exact, not merely similar: ListExtensions.UnstableShuffle walks i = Count-1 down to 1 taking one `rng.NextInt(i + 1)` and swapping list[i] with list[j] (ListExtensions.cs:45-58), and Rng.shuffle (rng.py:270-273) is that same loop -- which is why rng.py:290-291 already documents the equivalence for the map generator. No sort precedes it, so neither EV-5 nor EV-7 applies. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes_a.py ancientdraws`): the shuffle takes 9 event-Rng draws on a 10-relic pool and 8 on the 9-relic pool -- Count - 1 in both cases, on both paths. The Tri-Boomerang is appended BEFORE the shuffle in both, so it competes for all three slots.

guards.what: this unit is one of the events with a parity RNG branch, so EV-3 does NOT apply -- and the branch is CLEAN on every path (the check the orobas lesson asks for)
guards.maps_to: events/tanx.py:34 uses self.event_rng when present, falling back to the shared rng only in legacy mode. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes_a.py ancientdraws`): the draw count matches Count - 1 with and without the Tri-Boomerang, and the event offers no locked option, so the orobas defect shape -- NextItem over a list that still holds a null-onChosen entry, taking a draw the sim's branch skips -- cannot arise here. NOTE the `eventrng` probe in tools/audit/event_probes.py misclassifies this module as 'rolls nothing': its regex looks for `self.rng.<method>(` and tanx writes `(self.event_rng if ... else self.rng).shuffle(pool)`. Flagged in the stream report; the probe module is not this batch's to edit.

guards.what: AncientEventModel's Hook.ShouldAllowAncient gate (AncientEventModel.cs:195 and the InitialDescription swap at :147-152), which the sim's AncientEvent does not model at all
guards.maps_to: NEGATIVE CONTROL, EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes_a.py ancienthook`): AbstractModel.ShouldAllowAncient (AbstractModel.cs:2167) is a virtual returning true and has ZERO overrides in the entire game source; the only WaxChoker reference left anywhere is the block-message loc key itself (AncientEventModel.cs:151), and there is no WaxChoker.cs.
